# Mainspring

> A backend-agnostic local inference server. One stable OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible API in front,
> pluggable engines (llama.cpp, MLX, Ollama, LM Studio, llamafile, GPT4All) behind it. Build the
> local-inference control plane, not the kernels.

Mainspring is an open-source (MIT) Go server. It presents a single stable API and runs models on
pluggable engine backends, installing/running only what a requested model needs. Its value is the
layer *around* inference — fail-loud correctness, VRAM-residency-aware scheduling, multi-tenant
governance, observability, and verified OpenAI/Anthropic-compat — not the compute kernels (those are
MIT and already win; Mainspring wraps them).

## What it does

- One versioned API: OpenAI (`/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/completions`, `/v1/embeddings`,
  `/v1/models`) and Anthropic (`/v1/messages`, tool use + streaming translated).
- Per-model backend routing: one server can serve a GGUF via llama.cpp, an MLX model, and an adopted
  Ollama/LM Studio/llamafile/GPT4All model simultaneously.
- Model aliases: map a friendly name (e.g. `gpt-4o`) to a real model id (chainable, cycle-checked at
  startup); aliases appear in `/v1/models` and resolve on every inference path.
- Fail loud, never silently degrade: `/capabilities` reports the real backend, device, GPU offload,
  and effective context (never silently smaller than requested); `X-Mainspring-{Backend,Device,Warning}`
  headers on every response.
- VRAM-residency-aware scheduler: single-flight load, LRU + byte-budget eviction, KeepAlive idle
  unload, optional preload at startup.
- Standalone governance: API keys → named tenants with roles (admin/inference) and per-tenant request
  rate limits (429 + Retry-After) and token budgets.
- Concurrency + backpressure: per-model in-flight limit + bounded queue; 503 instead of latency collapse.
- Observability: Prometheus `/metrics` (TTFT, prompt/output tokens, requests, residency, inflight/queued)
  and an append-only JSONL usage ledger. Token counts are real when the upstream reports a usage object
  (non-stream body, or the streaming `include_usage` final chunk) and estimated otherwise.
- Opt-in, verified managed install: SHA-256-pinned artifacts, optional ed25519 signed manifests.
  Never installs anything unless you run `mainspring install`.
- Deploy anywhere: single static binary, distroless container image, and a Helm chart (HPA,
  ServiceMonitor, GPU node scheduling).
- Graceful drain: `/readyz` flips to 503 on shutdown so load balancers stop routing while in-flight
  requests finish.
- Request correlation: every request carries an `X-Request-ID` (accepted from the client or generated,
  echoed on the response and recorded in the usage ledger); an optional JSONL access log records every
  request (method, path, status, duration).

## Backends

- Managed (subprocess, opt-in install): `llamacpp` (llama-server), `mlx` (mlx_lm.server, Apple Silicon).
- Adopt-only (detect a running server; never installed): `ollama` (:11434), `lmstudio` (:1234),
  `llamafile` (:8080), `gpt4all` (:4891).

## CLI

- `mainspring serve` — start the server (flags: --addr, --config, --model id=path, --api-key,
  --backend, --max-loaded, --max-resident-mb, --max-inflight, --max-queue, --keep-alive, --usage-ledger).
- `mainspring backends` — detect engines on this host (system vs managed).
- `mainspring models` — list configured models and their resolved backend.
- `mainspring install <backend>` — opt-in, checksum-verified engine install (--url/--sha256 or a
  signed manifest via --pubkey/--manifest-sig).
- `mainspring doctor` — diagnose backends, config, models, ports, accelerator.
- `mainspring version`.

## Endpoints

- `POST /v1/chat/completions`, `POST /v1/completions`, `POST /v1/embeddings`
- `POST /v1/messages` (Anthropic, text + tool use; streaming translated, incl. input_json_delta)
- `GET /v1/models`, `GET /capabilities`, `GET /metrics`, `GET /healthz`, `GET /readyz`

## Non-goals

- Mainspring does not build inference kernels — it wraps permissively-licensed engines.
- No GUI dependency; headless-first daemon.

## Relationship to Hydra

Mainspring is an inference *head*; Hydra (https://github.com/ankit373/hydra) is a provider-neutral
router/trust control plane above it. They meet over the standard OpenAI-compatible boundary. Hydra
works with everything (Ollama, OpenAI, Anthropic, any OpenAI-compatible endpoint) and never depends on
Mainspring — Mainspring is simply the head Hydra integrates with best.
